AF Hassan Ariff with TM Shakil Hasan, Abdur Rahman, Advocates-For the appellants in both the above-mentioned.

Standard Insurance Ltd ----- Defendant No. 2 Appellant

full_judgment:
5. The plaint case, in short, are that the plaintiff as a public limited company incorporated under the Companies Act having it's registered office at 141/1, Segunbagicha, Dhaka-1000 and has been manufacturing cartoons, back board, neck board and other related products for over two decades. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are the companies registered under the Companies Act, 1994 and have been conducting general insurance business (Marine, Fire Miscellaneous) since its inception. The plaintiff has a factory at Kadamtali, Faridabad, Shyampur, Dhaka wherein cartoons, back board and neck board and other related products are being manufactured. There are number of godowns in the factory premises for storage of raw materials used in the factory. The plaintiff has taken cash credit (Loan) facility from Sonali Bank, Bangabandhu Avenue Corporate Branch, Dhaka for financing procurement of raw materials and their storage in the godowns in the factory premises against pledge and hypothecation. The Prime Insurance Company Limited, the defendant No. 1 (leader) and Standard Insurance Limited, defendant No. 2, having received premium, issued on co-insurance basis, the Fire Insurance Policy No. 1-02-0010-0002-524-12-2001 (Co-insurance) dated 27-12-2001 in favour of Sonali Bank BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, as mortgagee and M/s Maq Enterprises Limited (the plaintiff) as mortgagor covering fire, lighting, R and SD and malicious damage risk of the items listed in the schedule to the aforesaid Insurance Policy for a total sum of Taka 14 crores. Thereafter on 12-12-2002, at night, a devastating fire broke out in the godown at the factory premises of the plaintiff; wherein 1992 MT. of insured duplex board was in godown No. 32 belonging to the insured/ plaintiff M/s. Maq Enterprises Ltd. was totally burnt. The plaintiff lodged a GD entry No. 900 dated 13-1412-2002 with Shyampur Police Station, Dhaka on the fire incident for further necessary action by them as per law. The plaintiff has informed the defendant No. 1 M/s Prime Insurance Company Ltd. On 13-12-2002 (Friday) over telephone and on 14-12-2002 in writing about the incident of fire on 12-12-2002. It caused a damage to the stock of duplex board in the godown No. 32 pledged with the bank and covered by the Fire Policy No. 1-02-0010-0002-524-12-2001 (Co-insurance) in favour of Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka and A/C M/s Maq Enterprises Ltd. Issued by defendant No. 1 Prime Insurance Company Ltd. The defendant No. 1 has also been requested to take further necessary action as per law and usage in the matter and process payment of compensation to the plaintiff. On 14-12-2002 defendant No. 1, Prime Insurance Company Limited has appointed 2 (two) surveyors, namely, M/s. Rupali Surveyors, 19/E, Sheikh Shaheb Bazar Road, Dhaka and M/s. Jorip O-Paridarshan Co. Islam Chamber (13 floor), 125/A, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka-1000 to conduct joint survey and assess the extent of loss of the insured stores. The plaintiff has supplied all papers and documents as asked for and/ or as required by the surveyors in terms of the Insurance Policy directly and where necessary, through Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka to facilitate speedy survey and assessment of loss. Thereafter on 14-12-2002 the surveyors appointed by the defendant No. 1, have visited the godowns in the premises of the factory of the plaintiff and on 21-12-2002 submitted a preliminary survey report to Prime Insurance Company Limited indicating huge loss due to fire and also resulting from use of water for extinguishing fire by the Fire Brigade and others in the midnight of 12-12-2002 pending further in-depth investigation of the cause and determination of the quantum of loss as well salvage. Then the plaintiff has formally lodged insurance claim for Taka 8,16,72,000 against Fire Policy No. 1-02-0010-0002-524-12-2001 (Co. Ins.) issued by Prime Insurance Company Limited, defendant No. 1 through Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka, the Mortgagee, for the loss of insured stores in godown No. 32 as per requirement under the Insurance Policy, resulting from damage in the fire on 12-12-2002. The claim lodged under the joint signature of the plaintiff and the Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka has been sent to the Prime Insurance Company Ltd., defendant No. 1, vide Letter No. BBA/ GAD-1/ MAQ BIMA dated 26-12-2002 of Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka. The Officer-in-Charge of Shyampur Police Station, Dhaka investigated the fire incident as a follow up action of GD entry No. 900 dated 13-14.12.2002 and on 28-12-2002 submitted a report on the fire incident. A huge loss of stores in the fire has been reported by the police in their report. On 9-2-2003, Bangladesh Fire Service and Civil Defense, too have submitted a report on the relevant fire incident. They have stated in their report that fire has been caused by electric short circuit. They have assessed and valued the loss of stores in the fire in godown No. 32 at Taka 8 crores. The plaintiff as well their banker, the Sonali Bank, BB Avenue, Corporate Branch, Dhaka have almost continuously and diligently endeavoured by letters, telephones and through meeting at personal level with the ranking officers including the Managing Director to impress defendant No. 1, the Prime Insurance Company Ltd for expeditious settlement of the plaintiff's insurance claim. Defendant No. 1 has made promises several times but has miserably failed to act in the manner expected to them. They have attributed delay in payment of the claim during the period ending in May, 2004 non-receipt of Survey Reports from the Surveyors deployed by them, finally, after months of persuasion by the plaintiff. The Surveyors fielded by defendant No. 1 have submitted their Survey Reports on 29-5-2004 wherein loss has been assessed as follows: 

 10. The surveyors were appointed by defendant No. 1, the Prime Insurance Company Ltd deducted 10% (Taka 81,67,200) only from the payable amount of the plaintiff's claim for so-called deterioration of quality of duplex board due to 2½ years long storage in the godown. This finding (determination of quality due to long storage) of the surveyors were vehemently objected to by the plaintiff vide letter dated 21-7-2004. The surveyors on reassessment in the light of the plaintiff's representations of their previous finding on deterioration of quality have on 1-12-2004 submitted a corrigendum to their joint final Survey Report eliminating deductions (of 10%) from the total assessed loss. The net loss has been finally reassessed by them at Taka 7,68,72,540 of which 70% would be/are payable by the Prime Insurance Company Limited and 30% by the Standard Insurance Limited. Ms Engineers Survey Associates Ltd. and Argani Inspection Company Ltd appointed surveyors of Sadharan Bima Corporation, too have submitted their joint survey report to Sadharan Bima Corporation at about the same time on 5-6-2004. The surveyors in their report assessed and mentioned the loss in the above fire incident have been caused at Taka 7,44,92,367 (Taka Seven crores forty-four lac ninety-two thousand three hundred sixty-seven) only. The Prime Insurance Company Limited, defendant No. 1 on evaluation of the plaintiff's claim, police investigation report, Fire Service and Civil Defence Report as well as the final Survey Report (of the surveyors appointed by them) have admitted the liability as per terms and condition of the Fire Insurance Policy No. 1-02-0010-0002-524-12-2001 (Co. Ins.) as per their letter No. Prime/HO/FCL-90/12/2002 /2004/ 3727 dated July 17 of 2004 to Sadharan Bima Corporation with copy endorsed to the plaintiff-Company and in their Letter No. Prime/ HO/FCL -90/12/2002/2005/102 dated 10-3-2005 to Sadharan Bima Corporation have re-asserted that the claim of the plaintiff-company arising out of fire loss is /was admissible in terms of the policy and in the light of findings of the surveyors deployed by the insurer as well as reinsurer as contained in their joint survey reports. Defendant No. 1, the Prime Insurance Company Ltd have time and again assured the plaintiff that they have been making efforts to arrange for payment of insurance compensation in respect of the loss of the plaintiff expeditiously. They have, however, failed to make payment of the plaintiff's claim despite promises/commitments and have unnecessarily resorted to another pretext (non-receipt of concurrence of their re-insurer for settlement of the plaintiff's claim) just for making further delay of payment. The defendants had received the premium of the policy issued by them and they admitted the claim and are responsible for its payment and, as such, can't legally withhold payment of the instant claim of the plaintiff in any new pretext including their disputes with their re-insurer. They were finally requested by the plaintiff's vide letter dated 29-3-2005. The persistent failure to discharge their obligations first in the pretext of non-receipt of the Survey Report by their appointed Surveyors up to May, 2004 and till July, 2004 in the pretext of their dispute with their re-insurer compelled the plain-tiff to file the instant suit to realise/recovery of their incurred claim/compensation with interest thereon at the rates specified in the Insurance Act, 1938 in view of the fact that the Insurance Policy given to them does/did not contain any stipulation to the effect that their claim for insurance compensation is/will be subject to admission of the liability by the re-insurer or that the underwriter the Prime Insurance Company Limited could not pay the admitted compensation to the plaintiff without concurrence of the re-insurer. The loss due to fire has been assessed at Taka 7,68,72,540 finally on 1-12-2004. The insurers have defaulted in making payment within stipulated time as per existing Insurance laws. Therefore, interest on the claim amount is payable by them with effect from 1-12-2004 at 5% above the bank rate as per section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938. 

 13. The defendants case is that the defendants entered into a contract with the plaintiff covering loss that might have caused by fire, by way of Fire Insurance being Police No. 1-02-0010-0002-524-12-2001 (Co. Ins.) dated 27-12-2001, the terms and conditions are laid down in the policy document. Defendant No. 1 re-insured the said policy with Sadharan Bima Corporation in the terms and conditions mentioned in the re-insurance cover note dated 31-3-2001 and the obligatory fire re-insurance treaty between defendant No. 1 and Sadharan Bima Corporation. On 14-12-2002 the plaintiff issued a letter in favour of defendant No. 1 informing "Fire took place at midnight on 12-12-2002 in the godown under banks possession and has damaged the property there which is covered by your above noted policies. We shall, therefore, request your good self to kindly take necessary action in the matter at your earliest and oblige". The defendant No. 1 on the very day i.e. on 14-12-2002 replied to the plaintiff informing that the defendant is appointing Surveyors, namely, M/s Rupali Surveyors and Jari-o-Paridarshan Co. to conduct the survey and assess the extent of loss. The Surveyors Company asked for necessary papers and documents to the authority concerned, in spite of delay in supplying those papers, the Surveyors Company submitted a preliminary report on 21-12-2002 with a comment we will be able to estimate an approximate quantum of loss only after the completion of salvage operation and sighting of necessary documents which will be informed to you in due course. The Sonali Bank, BB Avenue Branch, Dhaka on 26-12-2002 issued a letter in favour of defendant No. 1 requesting the defendant to deposit Taka 8,16,72,000 as loss suffered by the plaintiff claiming it as joint claim of Sonali Bank and the plaintiff, although Sonali Bank has not been implicated as party in the suit. Sadharan Bima Corporation, the reinsurer also on 30-12-2002 appointed as Joint Surveyors M/s Engineers Survey Associates and M/s Agrani Inspection Co. Ltd to conduct the Survey for loss caused by fire with a direction to submit the preliminary and final report in time. The plaintiff and Sonali Bank were requested by those surveyors to supply the documents against the stock and the security guards during visit at the factory on various dates but due to non-compliance and non-co-operation by the plaintiff and Sonali Bank the aforesaid Surveyors could not complete the physical survey in time, lastly the defendant No. 1 sent a letter to the plaintiff on 11-1-2003 requesting him to extend full co-operation with the surveyors to complete the job smoothly. Unfortunately, the plaintiff and it's associates did not co-operate, rather they did not allow the surveyors to enter into their factory godown which may be evident vide letter dated 3-2-2003 by surveyors to the defendants with copy to plaintiff and others. The surveyors as well as the defendant No. 1 requested the plaintiff several times to supply the necessary documents and also to co-operate in all respect for conducting the survey but the plaintiff was although negligent. The reminders dated 12-1-2003, 20-1-2003, 28-1-2003, 3-2-2003, 9-2-2003, 10-3-2003, 25-3-2003 and 27-3-2004 will prove the negligence and non-co-operation of the plaintiff in smooth functioning of the survey and to dispose of the matter in time. The Surveyors, Jarip-O-Paridarshan and Rupali surveyors jointly submitted the final report on 29-5-2004 in which they remarked that the exact cause of fire could not be ascertained by them, they simply like any other ordinary person think that it is due to electric short circuit. It is stated that "short circuit" is not an act of god or accident, short circuit is contributory negligence. The plaintiff is liable for failing to take due care and diligence in maintaining electric wiring and installation. Thereafter, on receiving the report defendant No. 1 requested the re-insurer Sadharan Bima Corporation on 28-7-2004 to accord concurrence for settlement of the claim and cash loss payment as per insurance arrangements as early as possible but was regretted. On the contrary earlier on 15-7-2004 Sadharan Bima Corporation issued a letter containing reason refusing the liabilities in this subject. These answering defendants do not agree with the claim of the plaintiff's as because the subject stock was lying in heaps/ stocks in the affected godown for about two and a half year which was against the declaration policy. 

 16. The final survey report could not be submitted to Sadharan Bima Corporation the re-insurer, within the prescribed period of limitation of time due to un-pardonable laches and negligence of the plaintiff to supply the documents as required by the surveyors and total non-co-operation by the plaintiff. Had the plaintiff jointly supplied and extended co-operation, the surveyors could submit the report in time and in that case the re-insurer, the major liability holder could not refuse the liability. 

 20. The plaintiffs to prove his case examined Mr MA Kashem, the Managing Director of the plaintiff-Company as PW 1 and submitted documentary evidence which have been marked as Exts.1-15 and material Exhibits-I-III. Exhibit-1 is Bima Policy, Exhibit-2 is GD entry dated 13-12-2002, Exhibit-3 is letter dated 14-12-2002 issued by the plaintiff to the Prime Insurance Company Limited, Exhibit-4 some papers and documents of appointment of surveyor, Exhibit-5 is the surveyor's report dated 21-12-2002 and Exhibits-6- 6(Kha)-series are the (3) Police Report, fire brigade report and the statement of claim, Exhibit-7 is the report dated 17-7-2004, Exhibits-8-8(Ka) are the report dated 5-6-2004, Exhibit-9 is the letter dated 8-11-2004, Exhibit-10 is the letter dated 29-3-2005, Exhibits-11-11(Ga)-series are the letters dated 20-3-2003, 6-3-2003, 22-3-2003 and 31-7-2003, Exhibit-12 is letter dated 19-2-2004, Exhibit-13 is letter dated 30-10-2004, Exhibit-14 is the letter dated 5-12-2004, Exhibit-15 is the letter dated 29-12-2004 and material Exts.I-III series are the final report dated 29-5-2004 of Jarip Inspection Company's and final corrected survey report dated 1-12-2004. 

 21. On the other hand Mr Md. Masum, the Executive Vice President of respondent-company was adduced as DW 1, who deposed before the Court and submitted some documentary evidence which have been marked as Exts. Ka the authorisation letter dated 2-10-2007, Kha Bima Policy, Ga letter dated 14-12-2002, Gha Memo of Prime/ HO/FCL-90/12/2002 dated 14-2-2002, Uma is the preliminary survey report dated 21-12-2002, Cha Fire Loss report dated 30-12-2002, Chha-Chha(1)-Chha (6) various letters, Ja is the letter dated 11-1-2003, Ja(1) is the letter dated 17-3-2003, Jha is letter dated 14-3-2003, Neo is the final joint survey report and letter and Ta is Civil Defence Report dated 31-3-2001. 

 25. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Senior Counsel who appeared on behalf of the Prime Insurance Company Limited in First Appeal No. 332 of 2008 has submitted that the impugned judgment and decree is bad in law as well as in the facts and circumstances of the case and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. He has further pointed that the Court below ought to have dismissed the suit in considering the facts and circumstances of the case because the plaintiff-respondent has totally failed to prove their case by producing sufficient neutral witnesses. He has also submitted that the trial Court has totally failed to consider the subject-matter of the suit and admitted facts of the parties and thus passed the misconceived judgment and decree and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. Mr Ariff has further added that the Court below erred in law in deciding the question of limitation in favour of the plaintiff holding that the defendant did not agitate the matter at the time of hearing although the Court below stated that the defendant in their written statement raised the question of limitation and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He has also added that the Court below has totally misconceived the facts and circumstances of the case and upon surmises and conjectures arrived at a wrong decision and decreed the suit. Had the Court below carefully gone through the defendants written-statement, both oral and documentary evidences it can't pass such a mischievous judgment and decree. He has further pointed that the suit is bad in law and facts as the Court below held that Sadharan Bima Corporation, the re-insurer is not a necessary party. He has also pointed that the Sandaran Bima Corporation being re-insurer is under legal obligation to share all liabilities as per re-insurance contract between the defendants and the re-insurer and, as such, Sadharan Bima Corporation is a necessary party to the suit, however, the Court below failed to consider such legal aspect and apply its judicial mind in trying the suit and, as such, the Court below ought to have borne in mind that in the absence of Sadharan Bima Corporation, the admitted re-insurer, the suit cannot be adjudicated fairly and no fruitful, effective, executable decree be passed. He has also submitted that the Court below failed to take into view that the plaintiff did not give any break up or a statement in respect of his claim or to explain the same by giving any schedule. He has also pointed that the Court below arbitrarily held the view in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants and in deciding the issues he discussed the defence witness only and avoided the negative answer of prosecution witness and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He has further pointed that the Court below failed to consider that in the insurance policy there was no mention about godown No. 32 neither it was in the prayer of the plaint nor in any schedule and, as such, the Court below ought to have dismissed the suit. He has candidly submitted that the Court below committed wrong in not holding the view against the surveyor's report as it was not proved by any of the surveyors. He has also submitted that the Court below ought to have held that the cause breaking out of fire was short circuit of electricity, almost all the agencies opined in similar views, but actual cause is yet to be ascertained, these opinions are based on mere surmises and conjectures. Short circuit of electricity is not an accident but it is due to the negligence of maintenance and, as such, the Court below ought to have dismissed the suit with mentioning as aforesaid and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He has also pointed that the Court below wrongly held that the surveyors did not mention in their reports about the non-co-operation and non-compliance, the Court below avoided to take into view the series of letters issued by the surveyor company to the plaintiff for supplying papers and documents, which have been marked as Exts. Chha series and, as such, the Court below ought to have dismissed the suit and, as such, the judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He has also quoted some portions of the statements, which are as follows: 

 If any difference shall arises as to the amount to be paid under this policy such difference shall be referred to Arbitration. As to the determination of the alleged claim of the plaintiff-respondent different sets of surveyors assessed the loss quoted different amount those are: 

 a) Surveyors appointed by Sadharan Bima Corporation, namely, M/s Engineering Surveyors and Agrani Inspection Ltd assessed the alleged loss at Taka 7,44,92,367. 

 b) Surveyors appointed by Prime Insurance Company Ltd, namely, Rupali Surveyors and Jorip-o-Paridarshan Co who assessed the alleged loss at Taka 8,16,72,000 and the said surveyors in their revised report assessed the same at Taka 7,68,72,540. 

 36. Both the plaintiff and the respondent adduced evidences and produced only 1(one) witness from each side to prove their case as PW 1 and DW 1 respectively, but mysteriously Surveyor who surveyed and submitted the report. Fire Brigade men who were entrusted with the task of fire-fighting were neither produced before the Court nor examined. He further referred the special conditions which reads as follows: 

 40. On the other hand, Mr Mohammed Mutahar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1 reiterating the submissions of Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant has pointed out that those submissions are not sustainable in the eye of law. Mr Hossain specifically and categorically replied all the material points and submissions advanced by the learned Counsels for the appellants. Mr Hossain referreing section 23A of the Insurance Company Act, 1973 has submitted that in that section there is no such provision that re-insurer is the necessary party in the suit. He has further added that the plaintiff has no claim except the loss assessed by the surveyors. Therefore, there is no necessity of schedule in the plaint of the suit because the plaintiff in the plaint incorporated the whole survey report. He has further added that the suit is not bad for defect of party as claimed by the Appellant because against the re-insurer the plaintiff has no claim nor sought any reliefs and, as such, the re-insurer is not necessary party. He has categorically pointed out that the non examination of the makers of survey report has not made nugatory the result of the same and the suit, because the defendants in the written statement and through exhibit 5 and Uma admitted the claim of the plaintiff. He has further submitted that the Arbitration clause of the policy has become nugatory because defendants admitted plaintiff's claim vide their letter dated 17, July 2004 claiming the re-insurance claim to the Shadaran Bima Corporation. 

 52. In reply to the submission of Mr Ariff that Final Joint Survery Report material Exts. I-III was submitted before the trial Court but none was deposed in support of the report. Mr Mohammed Motahar Hossain, the learned Advocate for the respondent took us through Exhibit-5 dated 21-12-2002 the preliminary survey report which is in the paper book at page 87 wherefrom it appears that the defendants admitted the claim of the plaintiff sending a letter to the Sadharan Bima Corporation claiming 50% of the re-insurance money from them. He pointing out that since Exhibit-5 and material Exts. I-Ill are admitted facts and it was also not denied by the defendants in the trial Court. Now they cannot raise any objection denying the materials on record. 

 54. According to section 58 of the Evidence Act the admitted facts need not be proved. Herein according to Exthibit-5 and Uma are the two preliminary Survey Reports which have by both the parties been admitted in trial in presence of both the parties. Furthermore, material exhibits were not denied by the defendants in the trial Court. 

 55. So, we are of the view that non-examination of the maker of the reports, i.e. the surveyor does not made nugatory the contents of the report. So, in this regard we are of the further view that the argument launched by the learned Counsel of the appellant is not tenable in the eye of law as they did not raise any objection before the Court below. 

 57. Mr AF Hassan Ariff and Mr Abdur Rahman, learned Advocates raised a question in respect of non-mentioning the schedule in the plaint at the time of their argument. They have pointed out that without mentioning claim in the schedule of the plaint they cannot claim the fire benefit. However, in reply of submission above Mr Hossain, argued that the plaintiffs has no claim for himself, but he has only claim as per preliminary report and final joint report of the surveyors. Therefore, he incorporated the whole survey report in the plaint as claimed and, as such, there is no necessity to mention the claim showing separate schedule in the schedule of the plaint. 

 58. We have gone through the plaint as well as the joint survey report incorporated in the plaint. Wherefrom it appears that the surveyors and the experts jointly prepared the report and submitted the same to the concerned authority i.e., the defendants insurers and to the plaintiff, none of them raised any objection against the said report to the Court below. So, it is apparent from the face of the record that the proposed claim of the plaintiff should not be scheduled in the plaint as he has no claim except the statements of reports as claimed and stated in the joint survey report. Therefore, we are of the view that in exceptional case like insurance claim when surveyors report not denied either of the parties in the suit there is no necessity to attach the schedule in the plaint when the joint survery report has been incorporated in the plaint claiming the said money in prayer portion. So, submission advanced that there is no schedule in the plaint, i.e. there is no statement of materials which is not fatal for this suit. Such an argument can be made on as usual case but not for exceptional case like insurance claim. 

 59. It further appears that in the present case fire broke out in the godown, all the godowns were under the Fire Policy. Out of which PW 1 categorically stated that godown No. 32 has been gutted by fire. So, they did not claim the total properties which were mortgaged to the Insurance Company, rather they claimed specifically which has been ascertained by jointly experts and surveyors without any objection from defendants. Therefore, we are of the view that the report submitted by the expert neither vague nor require any formal proof by examining any of the makers. 

 64. On the other hand Mr Hossain replied the submission of Mr Abdur Rahman stating that before filing the suit there was an appointment of surveyors by the appellant who submitted the report to the Appellants and Respondent in that time defendant appellants did not refer the matter in Arbitration as per claim of the plaintiff respondent. Even, at the time of trial the defendant Appellant did not file any application for Arbitration, even, did not raise any objection in the trial, therefore, the defendants Appellant waived the provision of Arbitration by implication and accepted the process of civil jurisdiction and, as such, after the judgment and decree they are not entitled to raise the question of Arbitration in this court in appellate forum. 

 65. We have perused the clause 18 of the Insurance Policy from which it appears that there is a provision for Arbitration however, on considering the materials on record it seems to us that the provision of Arbitration has become nugatory by implication and acceptance of the Civil Court process and, as such, the same is waived by the defendants because the defendant neither in the written statement nor at the trial raised the question of Arbitration. More specifically we are observing that the defendant after obtaining the Joint survey report did not take any step for Arbitration. Even, at the time of trial they did not file any application under section 10 of the Arbitration Act before the court below to stop the proceeding of this suit and refer the dispute in Arbitration which is permissible under the provision of section 10 of the Arbitration Act, 2001. Therefore, raising the said question after conclusion of trial and passing judgment and decree no legal scope to decide that the suit was not maintainable as argued by the learned Advocate for the Appellants, thus, we find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocates for the appellant. 

 67. The appellants of the First Appeal No. 82 of 2012 by filing an application sought for adducing additional evidence we have considered the submissions of Mr Abdur Rahman the learned Advocate for the appellant and gone through the application on perusing the same it appears that both the appellants contested the suit by filing joint written statement. In the Court below DW No. 1 deposed on behalf of the defendant No. 1 as well as defendant No. 2. The defendant No. 2 did not raise any objection nor filed any application for adducing further evidence. Rather, accepted all the activities of the DW 1 and defendant No. 1. So, according to the provision of Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure without raising any objection or filing any application regarding same subject which has not been rejected by the trial Court so, there is no scope to allow the application for additional evidence in the appellate Court. Moreso, when the judgment and decree was passed as admitted position of the surveyors report we do not find any reason for additional evidence to enable the Court to dispose of the appeal.
